Ruth (sales): Heads-up: CelerityHealth wants a Private deploy POC. They need clear guidance for procurement: peering vs PrivateLink, how to guarantee a single egress IP for their IDS, exact minimal firewall ports, whether SNI/original client IP survive, and an option for verifiable client-ip headers. Need paste-ready bullets for tomorrow morning.

Marco (netops): Short answer to paste: Peering preserves the original network source IP end-to-end. PrivateLink creates ENIs in the customer VPC so traffic towards the connector will originate from those ENI IPs (network-layer source becomes the ENI).

Lily (eng): For HTTP(S) we support adding an application header with provenance info: e.g. X-Redwood-Proof: base64(hmac)|ip|ts|reqid. Customer can verify HMAC (we'll share verification key via handshake). This is stronger than plain X-Forwarded-For and helps with forensics. For opaque TLS streams (non-HTTP) you only get the ENI source unless you use peering or a local proxy.

Omar (security): Signed header notes: requires a shared verification secret (rotateable). It provides tamper-evidence for the header but doesn't prove device-level identity; for that you'd need mutual TLS from client to their ingress. If compliance requires network-layer source IP in raw logs, advise peering.

Marco (netops): Minimal firewall/SG checklist (paste-ready):
- Outbound TCP 443 to Redwood control plane CIDRs (we provide exact CIDRs in the handshake).
- If PrivateLink: Inbound TCP 443 from connector ENI CIDRs (provided at setup).
- If peering: allow TCP 443 over the peering attachment and update route tables.
- Allow outbound UDP 123 to a time source (NTP) or ensure clock sync.

Ruth (sales): They asked if Redwood can "give us one IP to whitelist". What's the clear answer?

Marco (netops): Pattern: have the customer NAT connector egress through a NAT Gateway or Transit EIP in their account. That yields a single Elastic IP they control for firewall whitelisting. We cannot allocate an egress IP inside their VPC for them; they must manage the NAT/EIP. With peering the original client IP is preserved so they can control NAT at their edge. With PrivateLink the ENI is internal but egress can still be NATed to a single EIP.

Lily (eng): Performance/scale note for the POC: if they expect sustained high throughput (>500Mbps) or many concurrent TLS streams, recommend peering + TGW + a dedicated connector subnet to avoid MTU fragmentation and ENI bandwidth limits. PrivateLink is simpler to operate but watch AZ ENI throughput limits. For burst RPS SLA we can propose a Dedicated capacity commit commercially.

Omar (security): SNI visibility: SNI is present in TLS ClientHello unless the client uses ESNI/Encrypted ClientHello. If their network does TLS interception, they must re-add signed headers after re-encrypting; otherwise app-level provenance will be lost. Paste-ready SOC lines: "Data: request metadata and operational logs are retained per customer-configured retention in the Private deploy control plane; full request payloads are not stored unless explicitly enabled. Keys: customer-managed KMS/HSM supported; we integrate with cloud KMS or bring-your-own HSM via PKCS#11."

handshake-bot: Handshake ticket created: https://redwood.internal/handshakes/CH-5021  - netops to upload connector ENI CIDRs, sample SG rules, and HMAC key exchange instructions.

Ruth (sales): Please drop the exact CIDR ranges and a minimal SG + NAT/EIP pattern into the ticket by COB so I can forward to their network team. Also will paste the signed-header example and ask whether they want the HMAC verification key.

Marco (netops): Will add ENI CIDRs and two sample SG snippets (PrivateLink and peering) plus NAT/EIP pattern to the handshake ticket by EOD.

Lily (eng): I'll attach a short code snippet showing HMAC verification and the header format for their app team.

Omar (security): I'll provide a one-paragraph security blurb for procurement about header verification, rotation, and threat model.

Ruth (sales): Great, thanks everyone 7: I'll send the paste-ready bullets to CelerityHealth and confirm peering vs PrivateLink decision on tomorrow's call. :thumbsup:
